chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari from Hamdan ibn Ishaq who said, 'I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) or it was narrated to me from a man from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — the doubt is from Ali ibn Ibrahim — who said, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:'
Whoever visits the grave of my father in Toos, Allah will forgive him for what preceded of his sin and what was delayed.

He said, 'So I performed Hajj after the visitation, then I met Ayub ibn Nuh, and he said to me, 'Abu Ja'far the second (peace be upon him) said: Whoever visits the grave of my father in Toos, Allah will forgive him for what preceded of his sin and what was delayed, and Allah will build for him a pulpit adjacent to the pulpit of Muhammad and Ali (peace be upon him), until Allah finishes the reckoning of the creatures.'
So I saw him, and he had performed the visitation, and he said, 'I came seeking the pulpit.'

key_terms.حِسَاب: Reckoning (accounting of deeds on the Day of Judgment)
key_terms.طُوس: Toos (a city in Khorasan, Iran, known for the burial of Imams)
key_terms.مِنْبَر: Pulpit (a raised platform or seat, symbolizing status and authority in the afterlife)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and blessings for visiting the grave of Imam al-Hassan al-Muthanna in Toos?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi underscores the profound spiritual status of Imam al-Hassan al-Muthanna (AS) in Shia tradition, linking his burial site in Toos to the intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt. The promise of complete forgiveness (past and future) and the unique reward of a permanent pulpit adjacent to the Prophet and Imam Ali highlights the eschatological significance of Ziyarah as a means of securing divine favor until the final reckoning.
